name: OCI artifacts
auth: READ permission is required to resolve metadata and bytes; DEPLOY is additionally required to publish. Supply an unexpired Access token in AW_TOKEN; Basic authentication uses AW_USER matching the token subject. Token scope must retain the repository permissions; a token cannot grant access that its principal lacks.
fresh_home: Use an empty DOCKER_CONFIG and a new pull output directory under AW_WORK. ORAS pulls into that directory, independently of Docker daemon layers.
prerequisites: Existing OCI repository and notes.txt file.

configure.code:
umask 077
AW_WORK=$(mktemp -d)
export DOCKER_CONFIG="$AW_WORK/docker"
mkdir -p "$DOCKER_CONFIG"
AW_REGISTRY="${AW_URL#*://}"
configure.note: Registry authority includes a port when needed. AW_URL must be a bare HTTPS origin, with no path. Configuration files remain under AW_WORK.
The pinned client receives runtime credentials; disable shell tracing. For automated use prefer its password-stdin facility if separately verified for the deployed release.

publish.note: Remote repositories reject writes; use a local or one-node federated target.

install.note: Native manifest/blob and referrer retrieval use the registry endpoint.

limitations: Examples use HTTPS. CI alone adds --plain-http for its isolated loopback listener.
Cosign can use the same registry, but key creation and signature trust policy are separate from this basic connection recipe.

contains: oras pushes, pulls, attaches and discovers an artifact
oras pulls an artifact and its discovered referrer through the remote
